name: Emeka Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for a side. Everything you say is confidential. Walk me through an ordinary working day.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Emeka Wagner, twenty-seven, a chartered accountant with a master's, and I lead four people at Bridge Quay Accounts. We prepare tax returns and accounts for small businesses and charities. I start with yesterday's ledger questions, review my team's files, and usually finish with a client explaining a receipt that looked simple until it wasn't.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you enjoy about it, and what gets to you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like coaching Tariq through a tricky return and meeting people who run useful little organisations. I use AI now and then for a first draft, after someone else has tested a tool, but I check the numbers myself. I'm paid low for this role, Ruth and I have a mortgage and almost no savings, and few similar firms are nearby. That is what I carry home, even on a good day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That sounds like the past six months at my desk. A drafting tool saves me minutes on client letters, but I still spend most mornings explaining messy receipts to a real person.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our clients that their accounts still need a chartered accountant's signature. I'd tell my team to use the tool for plain letters, then check every amount against the ledger before sending anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be glad not to lose a teammate, but the ordinary money problem remains. I'm twenty-seven, already a senior at Bridge Quay Accounts, and paid near the bottom of the scale. Ruth and I have less than one month of bills saved, and only a few accounting firms are near us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my four-person team on its current rota this winter. I'd use the drafting tool on standard letters, then ask the partners for a raise using last quarter's billable hours. If they grant it, I'd put the first hundred a month into an emergency account; if not, I'd save twenty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mostly uneasy, because the firm looks stable but our kitchen table budget does not. I don't need a new invention to make the boiler bill frightening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What showed you how thin the cushion is?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The boiler repair last February took the whole savings pot and another three months of repayments. Ruth teaches at the primary school, and her pay covers groceries and the train pass. We can't call two salaries a cushion when one broken appliance empties it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you approach the partners?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd bring my team's signed returns and the client renewal list to the meeting. I wouldn't threaten to quit because there are few similar jobs nearby. I'd ask for a specific increase and a date for the answer.

say: I would call **AI** a small help with client letters.
I would insist a **chartered accountant** checks every return.
think: My **team** may be safe, but ordinary bills still strain us.
Few **local firms** make a pay dispute risky.
do: Keep using **tested AI** for standard letters after ledger checks.
Ask for a **raise** and save a hundred monthly if granted, twenty otherwise.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about bills despite steady work.
S0.quote: We can't call two salaries a cushion when one broken appliance empties it.
fieldNote: A **boiler repair** exhausted Emeka’s savings despite two wages and steady accounting demand.
Scarce **nearby firms** weaken his raise request, so he sets a smaller savings fallback.

steps.text: Keep four accountants on the current winter rota
Keep using tested AI for standard client letters after ledger checks
Save a hundred monthly if raise granted, twenty otherwise

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our practice already has a bank-feed system that sorts entries. If it starts writing, checking and booking for us too, I can see what happens to junior vacancies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At work I'd say staff should help set the rules before software takes over returns. I'd tell friends it should make small firms more affordable for clients without leaving the people who trained on those files out of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could probably keep a client-facing job, but two of the four people I lead may not be replaced when they move on. That would leave me checking a machine at speed and telling younger colleagues to find some other ladder. I don't think a nicer title would make up for that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask to test the bank-feed upgrades on ten tax files, keeping a list of its mistakes. Then I'd take the results to our staff association and ask for a rule that vacancies are discussed before they vanish. I'd save fifty more a month by dropping the sports subscription, in case my hours are cut too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, more for my colleagues than for a sudden dismissal. My own income could still shrink if the partners decide one lead can cover two teams.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would you bring into the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tariq is our newest trainee and still studying for his exams. I'd sit with him over the ten files so he can explain the errors, not just click through them. A person who can catch a wrong tax code should have a case for staying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask after the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd give the partners the error list and ask what happened to the hours saved. If they only talk about efficiency, I'd ask the staff association to put redeployment on the next agenda. The conversation has to happen before someone leaves.

say: I would demand **staff rules** before vacancies disappear.
I would argue lower **client fees** can coexist with jobs.
think: My **lead role** might remain while trainee posts shrink.
Even my **hours** could be reduced across two teams.
do: Test **ten tax files** and record AI mistakes.
Ask the **staff association** for vacancy discussions.
Cancel the **sports subscription** and save fifty monthly.
feel: I feel **anxious** about trainees and household pay.
S1.quote: A person who can catch a wrong tax code should have a case for staying.
fieldNote: **Trainee vacancies** are his main concern because AI removes the tasks through which juniors learn.
The **ten-file pilot** supports a staff negotiation and a household spending cut.

steps.text: Test upgraded bank feeds on ten tax files
Ask staff association for a rule on vacant posts
Cancel sports subscription and save fifty a month

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 is only two filing cycles from now. The firm takes longer than that to decide whether to change a printer, so I can't see a tidy transition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the state should guarantee income while people move out of jobs that disappear. At work I'd ask the partners to show staff their plans, including who signs a return when a machine prepared every line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my accounting post to go in the first year after full AGI arrives, even though I'm good at it. Nearly everything I sell is thinking work at a desk, so the robots arriving around 2031 don't buy me time. Ruth's teaching job may last longer, but one teacher's wage won't cover the mortgage and all our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this month I'd stop the holiday standing order and put its hundred into savings. I'd apply for finance roles at the council while there are still vacancies, though there aren't many nearby. In the first year after 2028, if I lost the job, I'd claim income support immediately and keep the mortgage paid before any other large bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed is the word. I can make a short list of calls, but I wake at night doing the mortgage arithmetic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to your family plans?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ruth and I were going to start trying for a child next year. I'd ask her to postpone that until we know whether at least one wage can carry the house. I hate making our family smaller because a date on a technology card moved closer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill and job application come first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage gets paid first, then heat and food. I'd tell the council recruiter I'm chartered and can manage public accounts, but I wouldn't say that is a safe field forever. I need a bridge, not a promise of permanent shelter. The council finance vacancy would be a bridge to another wage, not a permanent shelter.

say: I would call for **income support** during lost accounting work.
I would demand an open **firm plan** before layoffs.
think: My **desk job** could disappear soon after 2028, despite my senior title and chartered qualification.
Ruth’s **teacher salary** cannot carry the mortgage alone.
do: Stop the **holiday fund** and save a hundred monthly.
Postpone trying for a **child** until one wage covers household bills; apply for support after job loss.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by job loss and mortgage arithmetic.
S2.quote: The council finance vacancy would be a bridge to another wage, not a permanent shelter.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches his accounting work in 2028; later robots offer no delay.
His **mortgage** becomes the priority after expected job loss also delays a planned child.

steps.text: Stop holiday standing order and save a hundred monthly
Apply for available council finance roles before 2028
Postpone trying for a child until one wage covers household bills
Apply for income support after job loss and prioritize mortgage payments

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets us see a few rounds of tools at work. I could use that time, though I still expect accounting returns to change by 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask our professional association to negotiate paid training and notice before job cuts. I'd tell clients we should keep a person answerable for mistakes, even if the system drafted the whole account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I don't think my present tax role survives full AGI. Five years could let me move into advising community groups on grants and budgets, where trust and meetings matter, before the desk work is squeezed. That is a route, not a guaranteed new occupation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask Bridge Quay to pay the six-hundred certificate fee and release me for paid study hours; if both are approved, I'd enrol this year. I'd shadow our charity adviser one afternoon a month if the firm releases me, then ask for a real client case by spring. I'd ask the association to bargain for those paid hours before the first role is cut. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my tax role ends, I'd apply for a funded charity finance vacancy rather than wait for a return queue that no longer exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can see what to do on Monday. The risk still reaches our income, and I cannot declare us safe on the strength of a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How could you pay for that certificate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The certificate is six hundred, which is more than we've kept in savings since the boiler. If the partners refuse the fee, I'd use the free local college seminars and keep asking for supervised client cases. I wouldn't put tuition on a card.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the new role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want the adviser to hand me a grant budget to discuss with a real treasurer. If I only watch a presentation, I won't have evidence for a future employer. By spring I'd know whether there is actual work behind the idea.

say: I would seek **paid training** through our professional association before colleagues lose their accounting posts.
I would keep a person **answerable** for client accounts.
think: My current **tax role** likely ends after 2031.
A **community finance** post could be possible with client experience.
do: Enrol in the **six-hundred course** if Bridge Quay funds it and paid study time.
Shadow the **charity adviser** monthly if released, and request a real case.
Ask the **association** for paid hours; apply for a funded charity finance vacancy after 2031 if tax work ends.
feel: I feel **anxious**, though I have a practical route to test.
S3.quote: I cannot declare us safe on the strength of a course brochure.
fieldNote: **Firm funding** and paid release are necessary before he can enrol without adding debt.
A **client case** by spring would test his skills before a later job application.

Shadow charity adviser monthly if firm releases him
Ask professional association to negotiate paid study hours
Apply for funded charity finance vacancy if tax role ends after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years takes me from twenty-seven to thirty-seven. I can picture a child at school and a different line of work, if I don't waste the early years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say firms should spend part of the savings on shorter weeks and proper retraining. I'd argue for a public training fund as well, because small practices will not all pay voluntarily.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the return-preparation part of my job still goes when full AGI arrives in 2036. But I have time to move toward charity budgeting or teaching new accountants how to question a result. Robots coming around 2039 don't extend my desk job; the useful difference is ten years of notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep leading the team now and set a hundred a month aside after the mortgage if the next pay review permits it. Next year I'd ask the local college about a paid guest-teaching vacancy in accounting, but only take it if the hours and pay fit. Ruth and I would continue our plan for a child rather than suspend it for a decade. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my return work ends, I'd apply for the college teaching post only if it has funding, suitable hours and pay that covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, though the long runway helps me breathe. We would still have thin savings this year, and I would need to make each year count.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes you consider teaching?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I enjoy showing Tariq why a number is wrong more than fixing it for him. A classroom might suit me, but I haven't taught a full lesson. I'd ask to try one session before I claimed I could switch careers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would have to be true before you moved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the college what a guest teacher actually earns and whether it has a funded opening. If the answer is no, I won't leave Bridge Quay for a story about future opportunities. The savings order can still run while I look.

say: I would ask firms for **shorter weeks** and training.
I would back a **public fund** for small-practice workers.
think: My **return work** still faces AGI in 2036.
Ten years could let me test **teaching** or charity budgeting.
do: Keep leading the **four-person team** and continue our existing plan for a child.
Save **one hundred monthly** if the pay review permits.
Apply for a **funded teaching vacancy** after 2036 if accounting ends and its hours and pay cover bills.
feel: I feel **uneasy**, though a decade gives us room.
S4.quote: A classroom might suit me, but I haven't taught a full lesson.
fieldNote: A **funded vacancy** and sufficient pay would make teaching a real option, not an assumed refuge.
He keeps **family plans** while treating the mortgage and thin savings as immediate pressures.

steps.text: Keep leading four-person accounting team at Bridge Quay
Save a hundred monthly if next pay review permits
Apply for funded teaching vacancy after 2036 if hours and pay cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. My screen work meets it straight away, while a mortgage and a child we hope to have don't wait for a better labour market. A year of income support, funded training linked to a real job, and a duty for firms to discuss cuts with staff would help. I don't want my younger colleagues to learn about their future from a missing vacancy.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who owns the savings when the software speeds up a return. Clients might pay less and staff might work shorter hours, if the partners choose that. I would want those choices written down before anyone calls the change inevitable.

headlineQuote: I don't want my younger colleagues to learn about their future from a missing vacancy.

A **2028 arrival** threatens his job and family plans; longer notice lets him test advice or teaching.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** reaches his screen work before he can protect mortgage payments.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **income support**, funded training tied to jobs, and staff consultation before cuts.
